description: The bar chart illustrates the sample counts for four essay genres — Argumentative, Narrative, Descriptive, and Expository — across two categories labeled “Open” and an unlabeled second category represented by a pink bar (likely “Closed” or “Controlled,” based on common evaluation frameworks in LLM studies, though not explicitly stated in the legend). The vertical axis, labeled “Sample Count,” ranges from 0 to 120 in increments of 20. For each genre, two adjacent bars show the respective counts: Argumentative has 79 (Open, light blue) and 122 (pink); Narrative has 80 (Open) and 87 (pink); Descriptive has 68 (Open) and 100 (pink); and Expository has 62 (Open) and 130 (pink). The pink bars consistently exceed the Open bars in all genres, with the largest difference observed in Expository (62 vs. 130) and the smallest in Narrative (80 vs. 87). The chart appears to compare the distribution of samples under two different conditions or prompts, possibly reflecting open-ended versus constrained writing tasks, as part of the EssayBench evaluation framework for large language models in multi-genre Chinese essay writing.
